hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% as inflation drives up ground beef, buns and strawberries
hero.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
Americans planning Fourth of July cookouts this year will face noticeably higher grocery bills. The American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey shows that preparing a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase from the previous year. The primary culprit behind these rising costs is inflation, which has affected nearly every item on a typical cookout shopping list.

The price increases are significant across multiple categories. Ground beef, a staple for holiday burgers, has jumped 5.5% in cost. Buns to serve those burgers have become even more expensive, rising 7.7%. Strawberries have experienced the steepest increase at 12.4%, largely due to damage from a Florida frost that impacted the harvest. Ice cream, another popular summer treat, has climbed 5.3% in price. However, not all items have become more costly. Potato prices have actually decreased, offering some relief for families planning to serve potato chips or potato salad. Locally grown corn from the Glades is another option where shoppers can find competitive prices.

Andrea Woroch, a budgeting expert, offers practical advice for families looking to manage cookout expenses without cutting back on their celebrations. She recommends shopping more strategically by comparing prices across different stores to identify the best deals for items on your grocery list. More importantly, Woroch emphasizes that families should focus on reducing food waste as part of their cost-saving efforts. She stresses that this process should begin with planning out your meals in advance, which helps ensure you purchase only what you need.

Local shoppers preparing for their Fourth of July celebrations shared their menu plans, which reflect traditional cookout fare. One shopper described plans for hamburgers with coleslaw, chips and beer for lunch, followed by burnt ends, mashed potatoes and fresh broccoli for dinner, though they noted they would be unable to grill due to living in a condo. Another shopper indicated they prepare hamburgers, beef, steak and baked potatoes for the holiday. These varied menus show how families are adapting their celebrations while working within their budgets and living situations, making smart choices about which items to prioritize for their Fourth of July gatherings.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes, fourth consecutive spending cut
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year Florida's spending plan has shrunk. The Governor vetoed nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, plus another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund. DeSantis said he vetoed items considered either inappropriate or nice to have, stating he was not trying to set a record after his 2022 veto of $3.1 billion in state budget funds.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and fund major cancer research initiatives. The spending plan sets aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. Among the vetoes, DeSantis cut $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officer salaries. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year budget. The Governor ultimately vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations.

The Legislature had proposed transferring $750 million into the budget stabilization fund to prepare for new requirements. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the state's rainy-day fund, and lawmakers added the potential transfer this year to ensure compliance with the new requirement. The term-limited Governor exercised his line-item veto authority to block the transfer.

DeSantis indicated he does not plan to formally lead any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals. The Governor said that while he might participate if asked, he would not be leading the effort or organizing committees himself. The budget takes effect as DeSantis nears the end of his final term as Florida's chief executive.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit on standby as hundreds of boaters celebrate Fourth of July
cards.teaser: Martin County maritime teams deployed two boats with medics in the north and south areas of the county as hundreds of boaters hit the waterways for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is expecting hundreds of boaters on the water celebrating the Fourth of July weekend. The unit has two boats with medics on standby in Martin County's north and south areas. Harry said the team is ready to help with everything from a stubbed toe to cardiac events, potential spinal injuries or other medical emergencies.

Boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is their top priority when on the water. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices.

cards.headline: Florida beach lightning strike kills one person, injures three ahead of July Fourth weekend
cards.teaser: A lightning strike at a Florida beach left one person dead and three others injured ahead of the Independence Day weekend.
cards.body:
A lightning strike at a Florida beach killed one person and injured three others ahead of the July Fourth weekend. The incident occurred as communities across the state prepared for semiquincentennial celebrations and holiday gatherings. The strike happened during a period when weather warnings were issued for strong storms moving through parts of Florida.

The fatality and injuries underscore ongoing weather hazards during Florida's summer storm season, which frequently brings afternoon and evening thunderstorms with dangerous lightning. Beachgoers faced particular risks as holiday crowds gathered along coastal areas for Independence Day celebrations. Weather officials had warned of strong storm systems moving through Central Florida during the holiday period.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
cards.body:
A record-breaking 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, according to AAA estimates. This marks an all-time high for Fourth of July holiday travel. Of those travelers, 61.4 million chose to drive, making cars the dominant mode of transportation for the extended weekend getaway.

Friday's rainy conditions created hazardous driving situations on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando as holiday travelers hit the roads. The wet weather caught drivers off guard and led to unsafe driving practices. Driver Ed Budd commented on the sudden shift in conditions, saying "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the challenging weather, many drivers continued their journeys. Some, like Jim Macfawn, remained calm and composed. "I have a lot of experience driving, so I just roll with the punches," Macfawn said about navigating the wet roads.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations for this Independence Day weekend. Travel experiences varied significantly depending on route and timing. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and encountered favorable conditions. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras reported. However, other drivers faced very different circumstances. Fernando Amado described busy conditions compounded by the weather, noting that "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather. I thought people were leaving yesterday, but today is the day when people are really heading up North." The sheer volume of travelers surprised some drivers. Jim Macfawn reflected on the scale of this year's numbers, saying "It sounds like a lot. I'm surprised people can afford all the gas."

For travelers still planning trips, AAA recommends strategic timing to avoid the worst traffic. Those heading out should aim to depart after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday. The heaviest congestion is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. AAA notes that departure location, destination, and travel time all significantly impact the driving experience on holiday weekends. With record numbers of Americans on the roads and unpredictable weather adding to the challenge, careful planning and patience remain essential for a safe holiday trip.

cards.headline: Juno Beach fence dispute at JB-7 beach access could cost town thousands
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say beachgoers are cutting through their private property since the town removed a fence at the JB-7 public walkway in 2023, sparking confrontations and police calls.
cards.body:
A missing fence at Juno Beach's JB-7 public beach access point is creating tension between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with a potential fix costing the town thousands of dollars. Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. With only bushes now separating the public access path from private land, Colony resident Lori Hill said the problem peaks in summer, with cars parking in private spots and people cutting through bushes carrying coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said residents remember when the fence made the boundary clear and that confrontations with trespassers have become recurring. "We used to confront them and tell them this is private property, and they would get pretty rude. So, now what we've just been doing is just calling the police, and they've been coming up and confronting them," Hill said.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. The council agreed to address the fence question during its budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk social media post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controv.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises a larger question about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back. It's unclear when a final decision will be made.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
hero.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B and a record 93.5% graduation rate.
hero.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County has achieved an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year. The district's sustained success reflects strong student achievement across all grade levels, according to school leaders. This year, 143 district-operated schools, representing 84 percent of the district, earned either an "A" or "B" rating, an increase from 120 schools in the previous year. The district also set a new graduation rate record of 93.5 percent.

Student participation in advanced academic programs has been a significant driver of the district's success. Eighty-six percent of high school seniors took at least one college-level course, including Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment classes. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree while completing their high school diploma. Superintendent Mike Burke stated that the rating demonstrates the district's commitment to supporting student success and credited the achievement to the combined efforts of students, teachers, school leaders, support staff, families, and community partners.

One of the district's most impressive turnarounds occurred at S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which jumped from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has led the school for 15 years after five years as assistant principal, attributed the improvement to curriculum changes implemented three years ago. The school modified its early childhood program, which serves children starting at age 3 and connects with kindergarten instruction. Students who participated in this improved program are now in third grade and demonstrating higher performance levels. Tata noted the school had earned an "A" rating two years prior and had narrowly missed earning a "B" the previous year. Beyond curriculum changes, the school refined its overall academic approach and challenged both students and staff to raise expectations. Last year's school theme, "Be the reason you succeed," reinforced the school's focus on personal responsibility and achievement.

Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to significantly improve this year. The others earning the jump from "C" to "A" ratings included Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary. School grades in Florida are determined by multiple factors, including student performance on state tests, graduation rates, and advanced coursework participation. Community members have expressed enthusiasm about Spady's achievement, noting that the improvement strengthens confidence in the school and the broader Delray Beach community. The School District of Palm Beach County's sustained high performance demonstrates ongoing progress in preparing students for college and career success.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the prestigious All-America City Award from the National Civic League, recognizing efforts to strengthen community engagement and civic health.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach is celebrating a major national honor after being named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. Riviera Beach was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement and were announced as a first-time winner.

Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council for high school students, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program providing mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." She noted that winning the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community rallies around man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire earlier this week. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke about the loss and returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn reflected on White's memory, describing her as a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants, played piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. The timing adds another layer of heartbreak, as White's birthday was the Fourth of July. "She passed just a few days before her birthday," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce breast cancer patient and surgeon speak out after insurance denial hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield for a reconstruction procedure using GalaFlex mesh less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, prompting her surgeon to call for policy changes.
cards.body:
A recently diagnosed breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Three months ago, Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. Clark had a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction planned, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, believes insurance companies should reconsider their stance. She uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Despite her insurer's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago, thanks to Billington. Anthem responded that GalaFlex "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy," though the company noted Clark has the right to appeal the decision.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation opens historic Crain Estate to public in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and hosting artists from around the world in the Peacock Arts District.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates from the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The foundation offers guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Art director Krystal Masters said the estate remains 90 percent the way it was when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and pre-stained glass that leads to the front patio bar. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their estate, including a gazebo shipped from India decorated with tiny peacocks.

The property gets its name from peacocks that have roamed the estate for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven birds that have since grown to over 100. Among them is Bob, believed to be the oldest peacock on the property at 60 years old and recognizable by his limp. Bob has his own bowls and is hand-fed daily by staff. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world with simple but elegant accommodations. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with Masters leading one-on-one classes where students arrive with zero experience and leave with a completed piece of art.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award

cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced at the National Civic League conference in Denver and recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson credited the award to the city's long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic participation programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council for high school students interested in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award reflects the heart and determination of residents. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents. Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another," Miller-Anderson said. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike. The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is designed to improve accessibility and accommodate growth in the city over the next 20 to 50 years. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the city has a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently.

FDOT is constructing the project in phases. Crews are currently widening Midway Road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The Turnpike bridge improvement and partial interchange are also in the design phase. The widening project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. Port St. Lucie resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged that construction has been noticeable but believes the expansion is necessary and will make it easier to get to work. City Council will vote on final approval to transfer the land to FDOT at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce breast cancer patient denied insurance coverage hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for her breast reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction to eliminate any possibility of facing cancer again. Clark completed the mastectomy but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to the denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers investigational with insufficient proof that it improves health.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction and remains considered off-label and experimental. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined. Despite the denial, Clark underwent her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago, thanks to Billington finding a mechanism to make it happen. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

cards.headline: California autonomous transit company proposes elevated network connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company with projects underway in Atlanta and California, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The company proposes an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying about four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept is designed to function like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without getting stuck in traffic or making multiple intermediate stops. Glydways estimates travel times of less than 10 minutes between downtown and the airport, seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport, and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions carrying estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile and argued Glydways would come in far below that range. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal and potentially seek competing bids.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man whose fiance died in Monday house fire
hero.teaser: Friends of Misty Dawn White have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after a deadly fire destroyed their Hobe Sound home and killed White on Monday.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help White's fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said. Fenn returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy to process her grief. She described the home as "completely a state of devastation." White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. Fenn said White was always quick to help others and loved children and people. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. Fenn noted that Mark previously lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday was July 4, just days after she died.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit on standby as hundreds of boaters celebrate Fourth of July
cards.teaser: Martin County maritime teams deployed two boats with medics in the north and south areas of the county as hundreds of boaters hit the waterways for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is expecting hundreds of boaters on the water celebrating the Fourth of July weekend. The unit has two boats with medics on standby in Martin County's north and south areas. Harry said the team is ready to help with everything from a stubbed toe to cardiac events, potential spinal injuries or other medical emergencies.

Boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is their top priority when on the water. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended for Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, contending that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that found disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. The school board retains the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, with the timing of a decision still unclear.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the Fourth of July holiday.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with South Florida drivers facing heavy rain and congestion on already-crowded roads. Friday's wet weather created challenging conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd said the weather was beautiful until it started raining and everyone forgot how to drive. Despite the conditions, drivers continued their journeys. Jim Macfawn, who has extensive driving experience, said he just rolls with the punches. Macfawn noted his surprise at the sheer scale of this year's travel numbers, remarking that it sounds like a lot and questioning how people can afford all the gas.

AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and reported smooth sailing with no traffic or accidents. Fernando Amado described a different experience, saying it has been pretty busy, especially with the weather. AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion, with the heaviest traffic expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach was named one of only 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of the community.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Miller-Anderson said winning the award brings back community pride and reinforces the city's positive momentum. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before scheduled procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark's insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for her breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and decided to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction to eliminate any possibility of cancer recurrence. She completed the mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, but it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients. While acknowledging no treatment is risk-free, Billington says the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Anthem stated that without FDA approval, the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy." Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football sets sights on state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for the 2026 fall season with a state title in their sights. After finishing last season with a 10-2 record and capturing a district championship, the team fell short in the second round of the playoffs. Head coach Jimmy Robertson credited the strength of his senior class, noting that most are four-year players who came through the middle school program. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To elevate the program, the Scots have intentionally scheduled tougher opponents this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning, saying the team wants to compete at the highest level and attract new talent. For the Scots, postseason advancement defines success this year. Senior Jack Whelche stated, "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs." Senior Edmyer St. Jean described summer workouts as motivation for the season ahead, saying the daily preparation adds up to positive results on the field.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, the programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse will host a full day of Independence Day activities including a pool party, live music and fireworks at 9 p.m.
cards.body:
North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County. The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, Giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida waives admission fees at state parks for America's 250th Independence Day weekend
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection waived admission fees at Florida State Parks from Friday through Sunday to celebrate America's semiquincentennial, giving residents and visitors free access to beaches, springs, trails and historic sites.
hero.body:
Rewritten Card Body

The Florida Department of Environmental Protection announced it would waive admission fees from Friday, July 3, 2026, through Sunday, July 5, 2026, at Florida State Parks to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends and family to enjoy the outdoors and make new memories while supporting public lands. The free admission applies to day use only, with overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals remaining at regular price.

Florida's state parks offer hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding across diverse landscapes including caverns, wetlands, beaches and springs. The park system also maintains historic sites such as forts, battlefields and archaeological sites. Three parks are excluded from the free admission offer: Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park. The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award, recognizing the state's investment in protecting natural resources while maintaining public access and environmental stewardship. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks saw more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated $3.6 billion in statewide economic impact. Visitors can plan trips at FloridaStateParks.org and learn more about Florida's semiquincentennial celebrations at America250FL.com.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes, fourth consecutive spending cut
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year Florida's spending plan has shrunk. The Governor vetoed nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, plus another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund. DeSantis said he vetoed items considered either inappropriate or nice to have, stating he was not trying to set a record after his 2022 veto of $3.1 billion in state budget funds.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and fund major cancer research initiatives. The spending plan sets aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. Among the vetoes, DeSantis cut $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officer salaries. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year budget. The Governor ultimately vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations.

The Legislature had proposed transferring $750 million into the budget stabilization fund to prepare for new requirements. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the state's rainy-day fund, and lawmakers added the potential transfer this year to ensure compliance with the new requirement. The term-limited Governor exercised his line-item veto authority to block the transfer.

DeSantis indicated he does not plan to formally lead any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals. The Governor said that while he might participate if asked, he would not be leading the effort or organizing committees himself. The budget takes effect as DeSantis nears the end of his final term as Florida's chief executive.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities celebrate America's 250th with fireworks, drone shows and parades
cards.teaser: Communities across Southwest Florida are hosting fireworks displays, parades and drone shows to mark America's semiquincentennial, with events planned from Sarasota's bayfront to Fort Myers Beach.
cards.body:
Fourth of July weekend brought fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations across Southwest Florida as communities marked America's 250th birthday. Festivities were planned from Sarasota's bayfront and Nathan Benderson Park to Manatee County, Venice, North Port and Fort Myers Beach. The semiquincentennial gave this year's Independence Day events a special anniversary focus.

Bradenton and Palmetto celebrated together with activities along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest at Riverside Park featured 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a kids zone and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the Manatee River. Sarasota's bayfront hosted its America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m., while Siesta Beach held its 35th annual community fireworks show, funded entirely by local residents, businesses and community supporters. Venice celebrated with a patriotic parade through Historic Downtown Venice at 9:30 a.m., starting at West Venice Avenue and Avenue des Parques and ending near West Blalock Park. The city's America250 fireworks show was scheduled for 9 to 9:15 p.m. at the South Jetty, with contingency plans to reschedule to July 5 in case of inclement weather. North Port hosted its Freedom Festival: Cheers to 250 Years at CoolToday Park from 6 to 9:30 p.m., featuring patriotic entertainment, family activities, food vendors, live music and fireworks. Downtown Fort Myers offered a free concert by Deb The Dynamics and a combined fireworks and drone show at the Caloosa Sound Amphitheater.

cards.headline: Delray Beach opens 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule as part of official America250 celebration
cards.teaser: Delray Beach marked the nation's semiquincentennial by opening a 50-year-old time capsule from the 1976 Bicentennial as part of its Fourth of July celebration, which draws upward of 20,000 people annually.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition for more than 50 years that draws upward of 20,000 people, is an official America250 partner event marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. On the Main Stage at A1A, the city opened a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule, delivering a half-century message from Americans who celebrated the nation's 200th birthday to those marking its 250th. At 6 p.m., a 60-foot flag rose at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue alongside the National Anthem and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society.

Beach events began at 8 a.m. with the 4's on the 4th volleyball tournament and the Star Spangled Sandcastles contest, a sand-sculpting competition presented by local Rotary and Kiwanis clubs with judging at 11 a.m. Creations were required to be patriotic, not political. Guided snorkel and scuba tours explored the S.S. Inchulva, a British steamship torn apart 150 yards offshore by a 1903 hurricane. Evening entertainment featured tribute act Let's Groove Tonight channeling Earth, Wind and Fire and DJ SoNyce on the Main Stage, with Digital Vibez performing on the East Road Stage from 6:30 to 9 p.m. A Zambelli fireworks display lit up the Atlantic at 9 p.m. Roads closed from noon to 11 p.m. on East Atlantic and A1A. Free FreeBee rides circulated downtown.

cards.headline: Marion County stages four synchronized fireworks displays across Ocala region for semiquincentennial
cards.teaser: Marion County organized four synchronized fireworks displays at sites across the Ocala region, each beginning with live entertainment and family activities before the sky shows at 9 p.m.
cards.body:
Marion County is staging four synchronized fireworks displays as the centerpiece of Marion Celebrates 250, the region's observance of America's semiquincentennial marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Each of the four sites will open at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors and family activities before fireworks at 9 p.m. The locations are Veterans Memorial Park at 2601 E. Fort King St. in Ocala, Wrigley Fields at 405 E. Highway 316 in Citra, Dunnellon High School at 10055 SW 180th Ave. Rd., and the Belleview Sportsplex at 6501 SE 107th St. in Belleview.

The city of Ocala is hosting Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park from 10 a.m., a free celebration featuring live music, food trucks, a kids zone and games. Ocala-based country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette will perform from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is also opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads and the Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties. The Patriot Parade will kick off at Southeast 16th Avenue, head up to Silver Springs Boulevard and wrap up near Southeast 25th Avenue, with veteran groups, local businesses and community organizations marching in the early evening.

cards.headline: Florida beach lightning strike kills one person, injures three ahead of July Fourth weekend
cards.teaser: A lightning strike at a Florida beach left one person dead and three others injured ahead of the Independence Day weekend.
cards.body:
A lightning strike at a Florida beach killed one person and injured three others ahead of the July Fourth weekend. The incident occurred as communities across the state prepared for semiquincentennial celebrations and holiday gatherings. The strike happened during a period when weather warnings were issued for strong storms moving through parts of Florida.

The fatality and injuries underscore ongoing weather hazards during Florida's summer storm season, which frequently brings afternoon and evening thunderstorms with dangerous lightning. Beachgoers faced particular risks as holiday crowds gathered along coastal areas for Independence Day celebrations. Weather officials had warned of strong storm systems moving through Central Florida during the holiday period.

cards.headline: Florida's Miki Sudo wins Nathan's Famous hot dog eating contest again
cards.teaser: Miki Sudo from Florida won the Nathan's Famous hot dog eating contest again, continuing her dominance in the annual Independence Day competition.
cards.body:
Miki Sudo from Florida won the Nathan's Famous hot dog eating contest again, extending her winning streak in the annual Fourth of July competition held at Coney Island. Sudo has dominated the women's division of the contest for years, establishing herself as one of the most successful competitive eaters in the event's history.

The Nathan's Famous International Hot Dog Eating Contest takes place every July 4 and has become an Independence Day tradition broadcast nationally. Sudo's latest victory came as America celebrated its 250th anniversary, adding to the festive atmosphere of the semiquincentennial observance. The Florida resident has built a reputation as one of the premier competitive eaters in the sport.

hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
hero.body:
A record-breaking 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, according to AAA estimates. This marks an all-time high for Fourth of July holiday travel. Of those travelers, 61.4 million chose to drive, making cars the dominant mode of transportation for the extended weekend getaway.

Friday's rainy conditions created hazardous driving situations on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando as holiday travelers hit the roads. The wet weather caught drivers off guard and led to unsafe driving practices. Driver Ed Budd commented on the sudden shift in conditions, saying "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the challenging weather, many drivers continued their journeys. Some, like Jim Macfawn, remained calm and composed. "I have a lot of experience driving, so I just roll with the punches," Macfawn said about navigating the wet roads.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations for this Independence Day weekend. Travel experiences varied significantly depending on route and timing. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and encountered favorable conditions. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras reported. However, other drivers faced very different circumstances. Fernando Amado described busy conditions compounded by the weather, noting that "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather. I thought people were leaving yesterday, but today is the day when people are really heading up North." The sheer volume of travelers surprised some drivers. Jim Macfawn reflected on the scale of this year's numbers, saying "It sounds like a lot. I'm surprised people can afford all the gas."

For travelers still planning trips, AAA recommends strategic timing to avoid the worst traffic. Those heading out should aim to depart after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday. The heaviest congestion is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. AAA notes that departure location, destination, and travel time all significantly impact the driving experience on holiday weekends. With record numbers of Americans on the roads and unpredictable weather adding to the challenge, careful planning and patience remain essential for a safe holiday trip.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce estate into artistic destination with global artists
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate, the former home of Jaxson and Mary Crain. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. According to art director Krystal Masters, the estate remains 90% the way it was when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with stained glass and a bar on the front patio. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character without commercializing it. Guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds, which have since grown to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old, who walks with a limp and has his own bowls. Bob is hand-fed every day and sometimes feeds out of children's hands during tours. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world and offers simple but elegant accommodations. The art lab provides classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with Masters leading one-on-one classes for complete beginners using mediums including sculpting and watercolor.

hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic to Florida roads
hero.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home during the July Fourth holiday period, with 61.4 million making trips by car.
hero.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling during the Fourth of July weekend, and Florida drivers are navigating challenging conditions as heavy rain compounds traffic congestion on crowded roadways. Friday's wet weather created particularly difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando, where rain made road conditions hazardous for the influx of holiday travelers.

According to AAA estimates, 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the Independence Day holiday. Of those travelers, 61.4 million made the journey by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations for Fourth of July travelers this year. The sheer volume of vehicles on the road has tested drivers' patience and skills. One driver noted his surprise at the scale of travel, remarking on how many people were managing to afford the gas needed for such extensive trips. Another driver who completed a round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday reported relatively smooth driving conditions with no traffic or accidents encountered.

However, experiences varied significantly depending on when drivers traveled. Some drivers described heavy congestion, particularly as rainy weather persisted and more travelers departed for their destinations. One driver observed that while some people had left on Thursday, Friday was when most travelers were heading north, creating bottlenecks on major routes. The combination of high traffic volume and poor weather conditions created unpredictable driving situations, with some drivers noting that wet conditions seemed to affect how other motorists operated their vehicles.

To minimize travel headaches, AAA recommends that drivers still planning to travel should depart after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to sidestep the worst congestion. According to traffic projections, the heaviest traffic will occur between 10 a.m. and noon on Saturday, and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. AAA notes that the time of departure, origin location, and destination all play significant roles in determining the overall travel experience. Drivers who can adjust their schedules to avoid peak travel windows have a better chance of encountering lighter traffic conditions on Florida's major routes during this busy holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Vero Beach buries community time capsule to be opened in 2076
cards.teaser: Vero Beach residents participated in burying a community-wide time capsule on Friday that will remain sealed until 2076.
cards.body:
Vero Beach residents participated in burying a community-wide time capsule on Friday that will remain sealed until 2076. The capsule was buried in a ceremony marking a milestone for the city.

The time capsule represents contributions from across the Vero Beach community. It will provide future residents a glimpse into life in the city 50 years from now.

The burial took place Friday, July 3, as part of a community effort to preserve the current era for future generations. The capsule is scheduled to be opened exactly 50 years from its burial date.

Community members gathered to witness the burial of the time capsule, which will remain underground in Vero Beach until July 2076. The event marked one of the final community gatherings before the Fourth of July weekend.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition comes with a higher price tag this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Inflation is driving the increases across multiple items. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, while buns have risen 7.7%. Strawberries, affected by a Florida frost, have seen the steepest increase at 12.4%. Ice cream prices are up 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, benefiting those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades offers the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies to manage costs. She advises shoppers to compare prices across stores to find the best deals on their grocery lists, create a meal plan, and focus on cutting down food waste.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, received "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach achieved one of the district's most notable improvements, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served as principal for 15 years following five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround by modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program three years ago, which serves students starting at age 3 through kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year, alongside Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, stating "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.
